full_judgment:
3. Writ-petitioners, K. Ashfaq and others, filed the writ petition before the High Court Division for giving direction to the writ-respondents to return the mortgaged properties fully described in the schedules 1 to 3 to the instant writ petition of the writ petitioners against payment in full in accordance with the judgment and decree dated 08.10.1995 and 14.02.1995 passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Bagerhat in Artha Rin Suit No. 6 of 1993 and obtained Rule Nisi in Writ Petition No. 4784 of 2010. 

 13. The High Court Division came to a finding that there was no illegality in issuing certificate under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in favour of the bank. The High Court Division further found that the leave-petitioners could not assign any cogent reason as to why the provision of section 33(6 Kha) of the Amendment Ain should be declared ultra vires the Constitution. The High Court Division then found that the judgment debtors' right to Possess/enjoy the mortgaged property and the right to sell the said property ceased after issuance of the certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain, 2003. The High Court Division also found that the judgment debtors having failed get back properties on payment of decretal dues after compromise decree and after issuance of the certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain, 2003, they lost the right to enjoy/possess the mortgaged property by their own action. The High Court Division, therefore, concluded that the provision of section 33(6 Kha) of the Amendment Ain could not be said to be ultra vires the provision of Article 42 of the High Court Division in the facts of the present case.
